events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Beast of the Sea

options.text: All lands are ours to be exploited.
We must protect our own lands from attack.

events.text: Your scouts bring news of [landmark], water that stretches as far as the eye can see. The locals tell stories of a beast that moves across the waves, consuming and devouring the lands that it finds with its insatiable maw. Upon hearing the story, your advisors greedily encourage you to imagine the wealth of nations to be taken if there really are other such lands across the seas.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Desert Peoples

options.text: A sample of their desert metals.
A collection of their stories and myths.
To learn their routes across the sands.

events.text: The desert of [landmark] is vast and inhospitable, and yet there are people who call the sands their home. Your scouts report meeting a hardy and friendly tribe of nomads who journey across the sands between watering holes. Your scouts present gifts of good will from [rival] and are offered a selection of boons in return. What will you ask for?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Eager Explorers

options.text: I am pleased they foresee a bright future.
We all must share the burden of discovery.

events.text: Young nobles of the [family] family are pleased with our decision to explore the wider world. They are certain the nation will reap the benefits in years to come. However, such expeditions are costly. Perhaps the [family] would be willing to contribute resources to this noble cause.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Fire of the Gods

options.text: The fire cult shall be built.
The are right. The mountain should be left alone.

events.text: Stories are spreading that the mountain of [landmark] was seen surrounded by a halo of fire, radiating a heat that feels like it is of another world. The Priests of [religion] ask for a donation of stone to build a cult temple at the base of the mountain, but the of [religion] argue that the fire is a divine sign that the sacred mountain should not be disturbed.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Look Upon My Armies And Despair

options.text: Force them into an alliance so that we may begin making plans to settle their lands.
Force them to pay a tribute in iron, in exchange for continued peace.
They may continue to exist if they provide food for our People.
We will not destroy them (for now), if they provide us with a steady supply of stone.
Continued peace between us may be purchased with regular supplies of wood.

events.text: An emissary from the [tribe] appears before you at Court, a mixture of fear and desperation on his face. "Oh Mighty One," he begins. "We have seen blood and fire in our future if we stand against you. Tell us, what must we do to gain your favor?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Married Away

options.text: This union shall herald a new age of cooperation and achievement.
No child of mine is joining some [rival] harem!

events.text: [character] has been seeking closer ties between [rival] and [rival] and has hit upon the idea of a grand wedding to commemorate such a union. [character] would marry the prestigious [character], in magnificent style at the palace in [city]. There is, however, the small detail that [character] is not without other wives.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Mountain Fighting

options.text: There is always a path.
The mountains are full of life.

tip: As leader: +10% Height From Modifier / Hill
As general: +25% Height From Modifier / Hill

options.text: I feel at home on the peaks.

events.text: The landscape of the [landmark] stands quietly rugged as you approach, the ice and rock of the towering peaks creating a pattern of sublime splendor. However, this trip is not to view the beauty of the lands. Your generals have asked for guidance in how best to adapt your forces to fight better in mountainous terrain. Traveling across the scree-littered slopes below the peak, you find yourself imagining the use of such a landscape in battle. Perhaps there really is something to be learned from these rough lands?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Mountain Minerals

options.text: The mountain is sacred, give access to the [religion] priests.
Order samples of the metal be gathered for research.
Our armies can use the metal and space for training.

events.text: The mountain of [landmark] is reported to have layers of an unknown iridescent metal folded into the rock. The reports of the mountain shimmering in the evening sun captures the imagination of [city] and soon a host of interested parties are gathering equipment to explore this new wonder. Which group will you favor on their explorations of the mountain?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Natural History

options.text: Give him the money.
[character] should fund this himself.

events.text: Upon hearing of [landmark], your Court Scientist [character] is unable to rest. He comes to you one morning, blurry eyed and excitably fidgeting, asking for funding to travel and write about the newly discovered natural wonder. Will you fund this undertaking to unlock some of the mysteries of this world?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: River Crossing

options.text: Bridge it rapidly with wood.
Take the time for a complex stone bridge.
The river is clearly sacred, we must find a natural crossing.
We will find another way.

events.text: The waters of [landmark] are swift and treacherous. Your scouts send word that it may be wise to bridge the river to allow easier access across. Your engineers rapidly draw up plans for two constructions. A wood bridge could be swiftly built and would allow swift deployment, whilst a stone bridge adorned with statues and inscriptions would leave a lasting monument to your legacy. What will you command?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Rivers and Springs

options.text: Bid the [unit] to carry word of this omen with them.
Erect a stele praising.
Use the site as an area for sacrifice.

events.text: The practices of [religion] often take place outside at natural features of special significance. The scouts who discovered the [landmark] showed it to some of your [unit], who say that they saw an omen of the gods there: A figure covered in red-ocher like the priests of [rival]. Will you claim this site for?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sacred Ground

options.text: The [religion] have a superior claim.
The land is sacred to [religion].
Convince the priests to share.

events.text: The discovery of [landmark] has the priests of [religion] and [religion] at each other’s throats, each arguing that the area is sacred to their religion, and theirs alone. The court beg for you to intervene before the argument breaks out into fighting in the streets. Which religion's claim shall you support?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Shadows and Dust

options.text: Our nation will last forever!
We must keep records for the future generations.
We will celebrate this wonder in art.

events.text: Hearing your scouts' reports of the newly discovered landmark, you make a visit to [landmark]. The natural wonder laid out before you makes the breath catch in your throat. It seems inconceivable that this world may have existed before your ancestors. Your mind races as you imagine the number of nations that might have risen and fallen in the shadow of this wonder. Before the awesome beauty you realize that even your nation must one day fall.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Studying [landmark]

options.text: Allow him to make his own way and make new friends.
Send a group of guards to protect him as he studies.
Have a break from administration and take the trip together.

events.text: [character] excitedly asks if you have seen [landmark]. He believes that studying the area’s unique properties could aid his studies, and points out that it is important for a potential ruler to explore the reaches of the realm. [character] seems set on going, what escort shall you provide?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Pilgrimage to [landmark]

options.text: Keep the gates of [city] open to all.
The pilgrims will have to find another route.

events.text: The followers of [religion] have started making pilgrimages to [landmark], claiming that the natural wonder has been touched by. The route passes through [city], now flooded with pilgrims. Additional traffic would normally be good for a city, but the pilgrims have been flooding the roads and slowing down vital deliveries of supplies and trade. The people of the city are becoming increasingly frustrated and send a delegation asking that you restrict access to the pilgrimage site.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Sea Peoples

options.text: We will take to the seas ourselves.
Study the artwork.
Prepare for any attacks by sea.

events.text: Your scouts report seeing signs of devastation on the coast by [landmark]. The ruins of what once may have been a settlement stand empty and abandoned, left to the birds and the weather. Reliefs on the walls of the ruin show a ferocious battle as an unknown force attacks from the sea, leaving devastation in their wake. No names are given for the attackers. Who were these mysterious people and could they still be out across the waters?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Shadows of [landmark]

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: The land is marked by death, it should be left alone.
Build a statue to the cthonic gods.
Celebrate the find with a holy day for.

events.text: In the shadows of [landmark], your subjects found a cave trailing far underground. As they delved deeper, the walls of stone hummed with whispers as the air grew difficult to breathe. When word reaches [city], the agree that this is likely an entrance to the lands of the dead, possibly the one supposedly entered by on his travels.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Wilderness Beyond

options.text: Marble to shape into great cities.
Ore to prepare us for the struggles ahead.
We will find what we need on our own.

events.text: In the wilderness beyond [rival]’s borders, our troops discover a small settlement tucked away in a valley. Though cautious at first, the inhabitants appear peaceful and are willing to trade knowledge. Familiar with the land, they offer to direct us towards resources for a small price. What does [rival] seek?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Those Before

options.text: We will adopt the laws of our ancestors.
Our ways are our own.

events.text: Ancient carvings have been discovered in a cave near [landmark]. After careful study, the learned members of the [family] family claim that it is a work by our distant ancestors, who once inhabited this region. It is said that they followed a practice where the eldest was the leader of the tribe. The [family] family encourage you to resurrect the practice in [rival], to pay respects to those who came before.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Voice of the River

options.text: Bring the seer to court.

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Cave in this pagan site.
Spend time studying the words of the dead.

events.text: Locals to the [landmark] tell of a small cave along the river-bank, where it is possible to call forth the spirits of the dead to hear their wisdom. The earth bears witness to all that happens on it, and in the hallowed chamber it whispers secrets to [character] through the music of the running water and the vapors of the underworld. Your scouts refuse to linger in this place of the dead.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Witch Queen

options.text: I can imagine learning to love a witch.
No marriage, but we can find a use for [character].
No witch shall ever enter [rival].

events.text: Tales of [character], the [tribe] queen, have reached the court, and we cannot help but find the stories of unholy rituals and prophetic fits compelling. A marriage to [character] would allow us access to her formidable powers, but it would certainly cause controversy.
